absent: Hash drop mechanics, negative policy values, mount prohibition lifecycle, and dentry sequence protocol details.
Filesystem release hook contracts, removal notification effects, and generic drop versus eviction internals.
Core single inode IO path, mapping writeback helpers, throttling, and superblock operation details.
Cgroup writeback structures, reference handling, workqueue completion, and switch execution beyond queueing.
Locking, atomic, once access, list, waitqueue, warning, and bandwidth accounting internals owned elsewhere.

findings.text: Fragments define globally linkable operations for dentry removal, inode reference management, lazy timestamp handling, immediate inode writeback, writeback control detachment, writeback completion waiting, LRU handling and waitqueue preparation, usable from other translation units.

Deletion entry distinguishes exclusive dentry ownership from shared ownership. Exclusive case clears mount prohibition and detaches inode while still holding both locks; shared case drops hash association and releases locks without detaching.
Dentry type is stored as masked bits inside general flags; accessor returns only those bits.

Unlink transitions a dentry from positive to negative under sequence protection, clears type and inode link, removes alias linkage, resets waiter state, emits removal notification when link count is zero, then releases inode through filesystem hook when present else generic release.
Clearing a dentry removes type bits with once semantics, nulls inode pointer, and increments per CPU negative counter only when dentry resides on plain LRU rather than shrink or other lists.

Reference release tolerates null, asserts absence of freeing states and positive count, fast returns when count stays above final, flushes lazy timestamps and retries, then under lock rechecks dirty time race and either returns on resurrection or proceeds to final handling.

Final handling consults filesystem drop hook or generic policy; cacheable live inodes on active superblocks join LRU and return. Otherwise it either marks freeing directly or marks will free, performs synchronous writeback, converts to freeing, detaches from LRU and evicts.

Lazytime synchronization is skipped when dirty time flag absent; otherwise it delegates to filesystem hook when available, else escalates to synchronous dirty marking and requests retry. Hook path clears flag under lock before invoking filesystem operation.
Checked inode state and count accessors require holding inode lock; once variants provide lock free atomic observation. Raw set and clear update state with once store semantics.

Immediate writeback entry requests full file range with unbounded count, selects full sync versus opportunistic mode from caller flag, disables data write when mapping cannot support writeback, allows sleeping, and delegates to single inode writeback.

Single inode writeback warns on unexpected freeing combinations, serializes on sync flag with wait for integrity syncs and early return for opportunistic syncs, skips fully clean inodes unless writeback tags or metadata writeback remain, then marks sync, performs IO, and afterwards either detaches clean inodes or requeues dirty or time dirty ones.

Writeback list operations require both writeback list lock and inode lock with list lock outer. Association changes use a retry loop that drops inode lock, takes list lock, validates writeback identity, and repeats on mismatch; simplified builds use direct lock handoff without validation.
Moving an inode between writeback lists updates global dirty IO presence and bandwidth accounting; membership on time dirty list alone is treated as not populated.

Control attachment is a no op when cgroup writeback disabled; otherwise it pins current writeback structure, records identifiers and byte counters, takes a reference, releases inode lock, and triggers domain switch when attached structure is dying for non dying cgroup reasons.

Detach selects round winner among current and candidate domains by bytes written, folds winner IO time into per inode average with fast first sample, ignores samples far below average, shifts time proportional history slots marking foreign wins, and requests domain switch when foreign slots exceed threshold before storing updated winner average and history.

Switch preparation rejects direct access files, inactive superblocks, inodes already switching or freeing, and identity switches; accepted switches pin superblock with barrier ordering, set switching flag under lock and hold an extra inode reference.

Switch initiation is skipped when a switch already flagged or too many switches in flight; otherwise it allocates a small atomic context, resolves target memory cgroup and writeback structure, prepares inode, then queues context to target with work scheduling on first addition.
Redirty clears queued flag, detaches freeing inodes without list tracking, otherwise refreshes dirtied timestamp when older than existing dirty tail and moves inode to dirty tail.

Completion clears sync flag, attempts LRU insertion, then wakes sync bit waiters. LRU admission rejects dirty syncing freeing or referenced states, non zero counts, inactive superblocks and unshrinkable mappings; successful insertion accounts unused count while duplicate insertion with rotate marks referenced.

Dentry deletion acquires inode lock before dentry lock; unlink path releases both after detach. Writeback waiting asserts inode lock, sleeps uninterruptibly dropping and retaking lock until sync flag clears.
Final count sanity check is acknowledged racy: two concurrent releasers observing count one can both proceed past the check.
Per inode foreign tracking fields may be updated concurrently without serialization; occasional inaccuracy is accepted.
Freeing inodes must not remain on or move within writeback IO lists; helpers warn on violation and detach instead of requeueing.

Observed inode state includes spin lock, atomic reference count, state flags, link count, superblock link, mapping link, IO list node, LRU node, writeback association with foreign winner average history and byte tracking, dirtied timestamp, persistent flags, data mapping and operation vectors.

Observed dentry state includes flags with type and mount and list membership bits, inode link, two locks with reference count, sequence counter, alias node sharing storage with waiter pointer, operation vector with release hook, and LRU membership.
Sync waiting uses address derived from inode state base plus bit offset to build a wait queue and sleep until flag clears; completion wakes same address with caller ensuring ordering via inode lock.

Clean inode detachment clears queued flag and depopulates accounting; cgroup aware variant moves node to attached list for foreign structures and removes it for root structure, while simplified variant always removes node.
